messages:
olivia: Bringing up cormorant-embed-1.0 on staging for embeddings onboarding. Quick sanity check results look weird after quantization, posting numbers below. Anyone free to eyeball? :eyes:

sanjay: paste the numbers?

olivia: baseline FP32 (wiki-holdout): recall@1=0.82, recall@5=0.95, silhouette=0.68
int8 (per-tensor symmetric): recall@1=0.78, recall@5=0.92, silhouette=0.60
int4 (per-tensor): recall@1=0.60, recall@5=0.78, silhouette=0.44

Command I ran:
```
./eval_embeddings.py --model cormorant-embed-1.0 --dataset wiki_holdout --metric cosine --norm l2 --k 5 --quant int8
```

priya: interesting, are you normalizing before NN? and are we using cosine in the index or inner product? small changes there can flip metrics.

olivia: vectors are L2-normalized and HNSW index built with angular distance (faiss metric=INNER_PRODUCT on normalized vectors).

mike: what quant backend did you use? per-tensor symmetric usually worse than per-channel for embeddings.

olivia: FYI I used the simple quant pipeline we have in infra: per-tensor symmetric with 8-bit linear quant. haven't tried per-channel yet.

eva: also double-check index build params — efConstruction and efSearch can affect recall, but silhouette should be independent. If silhouette dropped, that suggests embedding geometry changed (cosine shift).

deploy-bot: cormorant-embed-1.0 (quant=int8) deployed to staging, tests queued.

sanjay: can you run the anchor query set (the 200 anchors we track)? put top-5 IDs for a few failing anchors so we can inspect flip patterns.

olivia: posting a few anchor examples where FP32 vs int8 flipped:
- q: "python list comprehension" FP32 top1=doc_342, int8 top1=doc_120 (doc_342 moved to rank 4)
- q: "election polling methods" FP32 top1=doc_77, int8 top1=doc_88 (doc_77 absent in top5)

priya: those look like real rank flips. two possible causes: asymmetric quant noise on high-variance dims or outlier values saturating per-tensor scale. Try per-channel quant and also a clip at e.g. 3 sigma before quant.

mike: also try building HNSW with cosine distance on raw floats vs building on quantized vectors to see if mismatch is in index stage. Building index on quantized vectors can amplify noise.

olivia: good point. plan: (1) run per-channel int8, (2) rebuild HNSW on quantized vectors vs floats, (3) compute per-dim cosine shift histogram to see which dims move most. I'll run tonight and report. assigning to me + sanjay. ETA ~tomorrow morning.

priya: for int4 it's expected to be rough. OPQ + per-channel or group-wise quantization might help. also consider small calibration set for bias correction.

sanjay: if per-channel int8 recovers >98% of FP32 recall, we can accept int8 on staging. int4 probably needs a retrain/distillation path.

olivia: quick experiment results (ran per-channel int8 & rebuilt index with angular metric on quantized vectors):
- per-channel int8 on quantized-index: recall@1=0.81, recall@5=0.94, silhouette=0.62
- per-channel int8 but index built on float vectors (then quantized at query time): recall@1=0.815, recall@5=0.945, silhouette=0.62
- int4 (per-channel, grouped): recall@1=0.65, recall@5=0.82, silhouette=0.49

mike: nice, per-channel helped a lot. int4 still bad as expected. do we have throughput/cost numbers for per-channel int8 vs per-tensor?

olivia: latency: per-tensor int8 (quant kernels) median token embed time ~4.2ms, per-channel int8 ~4.5ms, FP32 ~12.1ms. cost estimate: per-channel int8 still ~60% cheaper than FP32.

eva: given silhouette recovered and recall close to baseline, seems safe to promote int8 per-channel for staging. we should add a note to onboarding checklist: run per-channel quant + anchor checks + silhouette delta threshold.

priya: +1. For int4, propose a separate experiment: OPQ + small retrain (contrastive distill) and see if recall gap closes. log a ticket.

olivia: filed onboarding ticket #ENGML-6521 with results and next steps (int4 experiment, calibration, and anchor corrections). Putting the commands and plots in the ticket.

sanjay: thanks, olivia. can you also add the per-dim cosine shift plot to the ticket? helps model team.

olivia: will do. adding a short note to the onboarding doc: "Run per-channel int8 by default, compute anchor recall & silhouette; if recall@1 drops >3% vs FP32, run per-dim shift and try clipping/OPQ."

priya: :thumbsup:

mike: great work — let's keep int8 per-channel as default for cormorant-embed-1.0 on staging and gate promotion on the anchored metrics.

olivia: sounds good. closing the loop here, will post final numbers after we run full holdout overnight.

sanjay: ok thanks, will watch the ticket.

(1799123610) olivia: overnight full holdout results: per-channel int8 recall@1=0.811, recall@5=0.943, silhouette=0.619. promoting to staging-default quant profile.
